headline: 登山紀錄片新片評論
context: 紀錄片《Savage Mountain》回顧了挪威登山家克莉絲汀・哈里拉（Kristin Harila）的故事。她在2023年以92天完成攀登全球14座八千公尺高峰，打破原本約六個月的最快紀錄，但在最後一段攻頂途中，她的隊伍遇上另一支隊伍一名受傷的挑夫，這件事後來為她的紀錄蒙上陰影。另一部新片《The End of Oak Street》，由《It Follows》導演大衛・羅伯特・米契爾（David Robert Mitchell）執導、JJ・亞伯拉罕（JJ Abrams）監製，講述郊區恐龍橫行的故事，劇評對這部片評價不高。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Former cross-country skiing champion, Kristin Harila had clocked an incredible mountaineering record – but then, halfway up K2, she and her team encountered an injured porter from another expedition … Why climb a mountain? Really, there’s only one answer: to prove that you can – to yourself, to other people, to the world at large. Is that a good enough reason? Not always, as demonstrated by this thought-provoking but ultimately not particularly revealing documentary about Norwegian mountaineer Kristin Harila. From the off, we know this won’t be a straightforwardly inspiring tale of an ordinary person performing incredible feats against all the odds. That, despite Harila being relatively ordinary – a competitive cross-country skier in her youth, she was working for a furniture company when she took up mountain climbing – and her indisputably incredible achievements. In 2023, she obliterated the speed record for reaching the world’s 14 highest peaks ; the previous fastest time was just over six months; Harila did it in 92 days. The glory, however, was short-lived. In retrospect, the experience was “hell and a nightmare”, she says. Not so much because of the climbs themselves – although the mountainside footage suggests hellish and nightmarish to be broadly accurate descriptors – but because of something that happened during the final ascent, which cast a particularly bleak shadow over all of Harila’s efforts. sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: The director of It Follows returns after the terrible Under the Silver Lake with a sub-Spielberg pastiche of big-lizard horror and domestic unrest David Robert Mitchell is back with his first film in eight years, this time produced by JJ Abrams. It is initially amusing but oddly inert; contrived, derivative, commercially driven and weirdly inconsequential, a Spielbergian mashup about dinosaurs running amok in suburbia that doesn’t feel like homage so much as a pastiche produced by an AI Spielbergbot – except, I admit, for the moment we see two dinosaurs enjoy the full, physical flowering of romantic intimacy. That is not something Spielberg would feel comfortable showing – for dinosaurs nor, indeed, humans. I was one of the frowning naysayers unconvinced by Mitchell’s madly indulgent LA fantasy-noir Under the Silver Lake , a giant disappointment compared with his breakthrough, the scary masterpiece It Follows . But at least Silver Lake had ambition and chutzpah. This feels as if Mitchell is going through the motions – someone else’s motions. We are in late-1980s small-town America; at one point, a character sits in a car listening to Steve Winwood’s Valerie . Ewan McGregor and Anne Hathaway are Greg and Denise Platt, an unhappy couple who live on Oak Street with their two kids, Brian (Christian Convery) and Audrey (Maisy Stella). Greg is ashamed of his failure as a breadwinner, having a humiliating side-job delivering pizzas. Denise is secretly writing an autobiographical novel about a woman planning to abandon her family. voice_text: 紀錄片《Savage Mountain》，回顧了挪威登山家克莉絲汀・哈里拉的故事。她在二零二三年，用九十二天完成攀登全球十四座八千公尺高峰，打破原本大約六個月的最快紀錄。但在最後一段攻頂途中，她的隊伍遇上另一支隊伍一名受傷的挑夫——這件事，後來為她的紀錄蒙上了陰影。另一部新片《The End of Oak Street》，由《It Follows》的導演執導、JJ・亞伯拉罕監製，講的是郊區恐龍橫行的故事，劇評對這部片評價不高。
